answer: Put the compiled file next to the library page, e.g. `Library/yourname/yourthing.plug.js`, and list it under `files:` in the page's frontmatter (`- yourthing.plug.js`). The memory says `Share: Page` publishes the library page and gives it a public URI, but it doesn't say the command uploads the `.plug.js` itself, so I can't confirm that it does.

[1] Plugs/Development/Distribution and Testing.md (Distribution: ship your plug in a Library)
  Distribution: ship your plug in a Library: Plugs are distributed as part of a [[Library]] — the unit of distribution for all SilverBullet extensions. You don’t publish the `.plug.js` on its own. You publish a library page that carries it. / Follow this recipe in your own writable space. Publishing also requires a configured destination. The recipe mirrors [[Library/Development]]: / 1. Create a [[Meta Page]] under `Library/yourname/Your Thing` with frontmatter that lists the plug file: / ```yaml / --- / name: Library/yourname/Your Thing / tags: meta/library / files: / - yourthing.plug.js / --- / This library adds … / ``` / 2. Drop the compiled `yourthing.plug.js` next to the library page — e.g. `Library/yourname/yourthing.plug.js`. The `files:` list tells the library system to ship the plug along with the page when somebody installs it. / 3. Publish the library page with the `Share: Page` command (GitHub file, Gist, etc.), which gives the page a public [[URI]].
  Distribution: ship your plug in a Library: 4. End users install it with `Library: Install` using that URI, or discover it through a [[Repository]]. / 5. Updates: push new versions of the library page via `Share: Page`. / See [[Library]], [[Library/Development]], [[Share]], [[Repository]], and [[Workbench/Libraries]] for the broader library system.
[2] Architecture/Plugs.md (Plugs)
  [[Plugs]] (built on the PlugOS library) extend SilverBullet in TypeScript, compiled to a single `.plug.js` bundle and distributed via a [[Library]]. Each plug runs in its own Web Worker sandbox. A lot of “built-in” functionality is in fact implemented as plugs.
[3] Plugs/Development/Architecture.md (Runtime model)
  Plug discovery: Plugs are loaded the same regardless whether they are “built in” (= shipping with SilverBullet itself) or user installed plugs: / On boot, SilverBullet effectively just finds all files ending with `.plug.js` and loads them. Built-in plugs live under `Library/Std/Plugs`, which is part of the standard library file system that is overlaid on top of your space.

Exact facts:
- [1] Copying a `.plug.js` will be picked up by the sync engine fairly quickly. After this happens, a simple `Plugs: Reload` will (re)load the plug. No page refresh is required.
- [3] This page explains how plugs are loaded, executed, and isolated within SilverBullet. If you just want to build a plug, you can skip ahead to [[Plugs/Development/Reference]] and come back here when you need to understand *why* something behaves the way it does.
